h1: Branding a second brewpub outlet without diluting the first
title: Branding a Second Brewpub Outlet | Craft Beer School
desc: How to brand a second brewpub outlet in India so it feels like the same family without copying the first: name, design, beer, menu and team.
teaser: A second outlet can double a brewpub brand or quietly halve it. Most of the difference is decided before the lease is signed.
standfirst: Opening a second brewpub is a vote of confidence in your brand. It also tests whether the brand is clear enough to travel. Here is how to make the new outlet feel like you without making the first one feel ordinary.
sections: The real risk of a second outlet

The first brewpub's brand grew out of one place, one team and often one founder who was there every night. A second outlet asks whether that brand can exist without all three. If the brand lives only in the founder's head and the original room, the new outlet becomes a pale copy. Some regulars start to feel the first one is less special too.

The opposite mistake is just as common: the second outlet gets a completely new look and name. The brand you spent years building does none of the work.
Write down what the brand is first

Before any design work, write down what makes the first brewpub yours. Leave the décor aside and list the things a guest feels: the beer style you are known for, the tone of the staff, the music, the food, the price level, the crowd. Our guide to brand personality and touchpoints is a useful framework.

Then separate the list into two columns. Fixed: what must be the same in every outlet. Flexible: what can adapt to a new city, neighbourhood or crowd. This list becomes the brief for the new outlet.

Most brewpub groups in India keep one name across outlets, sometimes with the area or city attached. That uses the brand you have built and makes marketing simpler. It works when the experience will genuinely be the same.

A different name makes sense when the new outlet is a different concept: a beer garden instead of a gastropub, a small tap room instead of a large brewpub or a much more premium offer. Then the question is how visibly to link it to the parent brand. Our guide to branded house or house of brands covers this decision.

Check trademarks and licences either way. A name that is free in one state may be registered by someone else in another. Excise licences are issued per premises.
Design: family resemblance, not a copy

The new outlet should feel like a sibling. Keep the logo, core colours, type and key signature elements, such as the tap wall, the bar shape or a recurring material. Let the layout, art and some details respond to the building and neighbourhood. A heritage building in Pune and a tech park unit in Hyderabad cannot look the same without one of them feeling fake.

Our guide to taproom design that sells covers layout principles that should carry across both sites.

The beer is the brand. If the flagship tastes different at the second outlet, regulars notice at once. That is a brewing problem as much as a branding one: the same recipe on a different brewhouse, with different water, will drift unless the brewers control it carefully. Use the same specifications, measure the same parameters and run side by side tastings of both outlets' beer regularly.

Give each outlet a few local specials to keep things interesting. Keep the core range identical in name, description and pour.

Guests feel a brand through the staff more than through the walls. Move a few experienced people from the first outlet to the second for opening. Write down service standards, how each beer is described and how staff handle common situations. Train the new team in the first outlet before they open the second.

A small taproom detail: the way staff describe the flagship beer at the table is often the most consistent brand signal a group has. Give every server the same one-line description and test it on opening week.

Opening a second site pulls the founder's attention away from the first, which is when standards slip. Plan for it: a strong manager at the original outlet, regular visits and a clear way to track quality and reviews at both. Celebrate the original as the home of the brand, with something only it offers, such as a brewery tour or the full experimental tap list. That keeps loyal regulars feeling valued rather than left behind.

Read reviews from both outlets side by side every month. If guests at the new site describe the place in words your regulars would never use, the brand has drifted. That is easier to fix in month two than in year two.
faqs: Should a second brewpub outlet use the same name?
Usually yes, if the experience will be the same. A different concept may justify a new name, linked to the parent brand as visibly as suits the strategy.
How do we keep beer consistent across two brewpubs?
Use the same specifications, measure the same parameters and taste both outlets' beer side by side regularly. Different brewhouses and water drift unless controlled.
Do we need a new licence for a second outlet?
Yes, excise and other licences are generally issued per premises. Work with a licensing consultant in the relevant state.
